newsitem.title: USA: Anti-tax, wage hike measures fail in Houston vote.
newsitem.headline: Anti-tax, wage hike measures fail in Houston vote.

text.p: Local initiatives to raise the minimum wage and limit City Hall's ability to increase taxes were defeated by overwhelming margins in a citywide election on Saturday.

So-called Proposition A would have required voter approval of most proposed hikes in taxes or city fees, but, with all but a handful of voting precincts reporting, it was failing by a margin of 62-38 percent.
The proposal, put forth by anti-tax groups, was portrayed as a threat to the city's bond ratings by opponents, who were led by Mayor Bob Lanier.
Also losing badly was a proposal to raise the minimum wage in Houston to $6.50 an hour, well above the current federal minimum of $4.75 an hour. Voters rejected it by a margin of 76-24 percent.
Business groups opposed the wage initiative, which was the brainchild of organized labor, saying it would have resulted in a loss of jobs.
